prompt: A hiring-screening pilot uses AI recommendations for a human reviewer. An applicant appeals a rejection, and the organization must reconstruct who approved it and which model result informed the review. Which control best meets that need?
constraints: A human reviewer keeps final authority.
The disputed decision and its evidence must be reconstructable.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Assign an owner; retain protected case records linking model evidence to reviewer and decision, and monitor appeals for escalation.
Track only aggregate accuracy and defer individual appeal review until the next scheduled model update.
Keep the model output and let the vendor decide all appeals without recording the organization’s reviewer decision.
Record the reviewer’s final choice but discard the model evidence immediately after submission.

feedback.reason: A case-level record links the model evidence to the accountable human decision. Aggregate accuracy cannot reconstruct this applicant’s appeal, and the provider does not assume the organization’s responsibility.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability assigns people responsibility for decisions and makes the evidence and review path traceable.
details.scenarioApplication: For this appeal, retain the model result, reviewer decision, and escalation outcome under an accountable owner so the organization can reconstruct the case.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because aggregate metrics can reveal overall quality changes, but they cannot explain this applicant’s decision or resolve the appeal.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Audit detail should be proportionate to decision impact and protected with access controls; logging every raw input indefinitely is not required.
details.transfer: For low-impact drafts, a lighter review record may be proportionate, while consequential decisions still need an accountable review path.

messages.text: Aggregate metrics can reveal overall quality changes, but they cannot explain this applicant’s decision or resolve the appeal.
A provider can support the service, but the organization still owns its consequential decision and needs a review record.
A final choice without the evidence considered cannot show how the reviewer reached the disputed outcome.

prompt: A benefits-triage service rejects some model responses because required fields are missing. Rejected cases stop before a caseworker sees them. Which accountability arrangement should the service owner establish?
constraints: The response schema is checked before a decision is delivered.
Rejected cases can delay a person’s benefit review.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Validate the schema and assume the downstream consumer will recover every rejected case on its own.
Name an owner to review each rejected case, monitor the rise, and escalate sustained increases.
Ask the model provider to own every rejected case because the response came from its model.
Review model accuracy quarterly and leave schema rejections out of service monitoring.

feedback.reason: A schema check detects a technical failure, but a named owner and escalation path make sure affected people and recurring failures receive attention.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability requires a named person or team to own risks, monitor failures, and act when the intended service outcome is not delivered.
details.scenarioApplication: The service owner should assign a named operations owner to monitor schema-rejection rates, review affected cases, and escalate a sustained increase.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because validation identifies malformed data but does not assign anyone to resolve the resulting service gap.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A single malformed response can be handled through the normal review path; escalation thresholds should reflect volume and impact rather than every transient event.
details.transfer: For any automated workflow, identify who reviews failed or delayed cases and what observable signal starts escalation.

messages.text: Validation identifies malformed data but does not assign anyone to resolve the resulting service gap.
The provider may help diagnose output quality, but the service operator remains accountable for case handling.
Accuracy does not show whether required fields were missing or whether a person’s case was delayed.

prompt: A school-support assistant receives an audio format its current transcription path does not support. Staff need a reliable way to decide whether the input can be handled and who resolves recurring unsupported requests. Which governance control fits?
constraints: The current workflow has a defined supported-input boundary.
Staff must be able to escalate unsupported requests.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Send the audio through the usual path and let staff infer whether the resulting transcript is complete.
Run a single acceptance test before launch and treat it as sufficient for all future audio formats.
Assign an owner to review unsupported inputs and publish a safe alternative or escalation path.
Transfer responsibility for staff guidance to the transcription provider and omit a local escalation owner.

feedback.reason: A support owner and escalation path address the governance question. Silently treating unsupported audio as ordinary input or relying on a one-time test would leave recurring failures unmanaged.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability names the people who govern a system and the path for handling risks outside its approved use.
details.scenarioApplication: A designated service owner can review unsupported-input reports, decide whether the workflow should change, and make sure staff receive a safe alternative path.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because an unsupported input does not become safe or usable merely because the usual workflow returned text.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Escalation does not mean every unsupported file requires model retraining; some requests should be redirected to a supported workflow.
details.transfer: When a system encounters an input outside its defined use, make the responsible owner and safe next step visible to the people operating it.

messages.text: An unsupported input does not become safe or usable merely because the usual workflow returned text.
A one-time test does not identify who responds when new unsupported formats appear in use.
Provider documentation can inform staff, but the organization still needs an accountable operating contact.

prompt: A customer-service classifier routes complaints to different teams. A recent review found that some high-impact complaints were assigned to the wrong queue. Before continued use, which ownership control is most appropriate?
constraints: Misrouted high-impact complaints can delay customer support.
A human team can review routing outcomes.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Configure the classifier once and treat the selected categories as approved until the next annual renewal.
Send every misrouted complaint to the model vendor and leave local support ownership unchanged.
Wait for a customer to complain before assigning someone to review classifier performance.
Name an owner to review routing errors, monitor outcomes, and coordinate corrections with support.

feedback.reason: The classifier affects access to timely support, so its operating owner needs a way to monitor and correct outcomes. Merely configuring the model or delegating responsibility to its provider leaves the service response unowned.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountable deployment assigns an owner who reviews system outcomes and can respond when intended use creates harm.
details.scenarioApplication: A named service owner should oversee routing-quality monitoring and coordinate correction with the support team when high-impact complaints are misrouted.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because initial configuration does not provide an owner or a way to respond to harmful routing errors.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Monitoring can be risk-based; low-impact routing errors may use sampling while high-impact cases receive prompt review.
details.transfer: For an AI-assisted routing decision, establish who reviews harmful outcomes and who can change or suspend the workflow.

messages.text: Initial configuration does not provide an owner or a way to respond to harmful routing errors.
A vendor may help investigate, but only the service team can ensure the customer receives timely follow-up.
Complaint-driven discovery misses errors that customers cannot identify or report.

prompt: An inspection model’s false-negative rate rises for equipment inspected after a sensor replacement. A reliability lead must decide who watches the change and when affected inspections are reviewed. Which control is appropriate?
constraints: The change is concentrated in inspections after the sensor replacement.
A missed defect can create a safety risk.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Assign the inspection owner to track post-replacement misses and escalate when the cohort threshold is crossed.
Continue using the model while its overall accuracy remains within the original launch target.
Ask the sensor manufacturer to approve the model’s continued use without reviewing inspection outcomes.
Wait for field reports of missed defects before adding any post-change monitoring.

feedback.reason: The observed cohort shift gives the owner a specific risk signal to monitor. A generic overall metric or one-time pre-release approval could miss the changed inspection conditions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Lifecycle accountability includes monitoring performance after changes and assigning owners to investigate harmful shifts.
details.scenarioApplication: The inspection owner should compare the affected cohort, set a review threshold for the increased misses, and escalate before the model is relied on for that cohort.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because an overall average can hide a concentrated rise in misses for the changed inspection cohort.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A threshold should trigger investigation and proportionate review; it does not prove every post-replacement result is wrong.
details.transfer: When a deployment condition changes, name the owner, cohort signal, and escalation threshold before relying on the changed workflow.

messages.text: An overall average can hide a concentrated rise in misses for the changed inspection cohort.
The equipment vendor may explain the sensor change, but does not own the inspection decision or its monitoring.
Waiting for a missed defect to be reported delays action on an already observed risk signal.

prompt: A lending pre-screen is moving from a portal experiment to a client application used by more applicants. Which governance arrangement should be in place before that release?
constraints: The workflow influences access to lending review.
The move changes the number and context of users.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Treat the successful portal experiment as permanent approval for every client rollout.
Name a release owner, monitor rollout outcomes, and define incident escalation or rollback.
Let the model provider approve the lending rollout and handle applicant incidents.
Expand access first and assign an incident contact only if applicants report a problem.

feedback.reason: A broader client release changes the operating context of a consequential screening workflow. A release owner and incident path make the change reviewable and actionable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability requires clear human ownership for system changes, operational monitoring, and response to incidents.
details.scenarioApplication: A named release owner should approve the governed rollout, monitor outcomes after the move, and coordinate escalation or rollback if harmful failures appear.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because a limited experiment does not establish ownership or monitoring for the broader operating context.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Approval does not require a particular cloud deployment tool; the control is named responsibility and a defined response path.
details.transfer: Before expanding a consequential AI pilot, identify who approves the change, watches outcomes, and can pause or escalate use.

messages.text: A limited experiment does not establish ownership or monitoring for the broader operating context.
The provider can supply technical support, but the lending organization owns release and applicant response.
A response path prepared after harm appears leaves the team without accountable action during rollout.

prompt: A medical intake assistant’s diagnostic logs contain full patient messages even though support staff need only error codes and a trace identifier. Who should own the correction, and what governance action should follow?
constraints: Full message text is unnecessary for the stated troubleshooting task.
The logs contain sensitive patient information.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Disable all diagnostics and assume the sensitive-data risk is resolved without checking service recovery needs.
Ask the model provider to decide what patient data the organization should retain in its own logs.
Assign a privacy owner to minimize logs and review diagnostic access and retention.
Keep full messages in storage but hide them from the default support screen.

feedback.reason: The observed leak is caused by retaining more sensitive content than troubleshooting requires. An accountable owner must implement and verify minimization, not simply hide logs or transfer responsibility.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Privacy-respecting responsible AI limits collection and retention to what is needed and assigns people to oversee sensitive-data handling.
details.scenarioApplication: A named privacy or service owner should remove unnecessary message text from diagnostic logs, define the minimum trace data, and review access and retention practices.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because removing every diagnostic signal may obstruct safe operations and does not document how the existing exposure is corrected.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A trace identifier and narrowly selected error details may still be useful; minimizing data does not mean disabling all diagnostics.
details.transfer: For sensitive workflows, identify the data actually needed for the purpose and the person responsible for checking collection, access, and retention.

messages.text: Removing every diagnostic signal may obstruct safe operations and does not document how the existing exposure is corrected.
Provider guidance can help, but the organization controls its logs and remains accountable for its data practices.
A display mask does not minimize the sensitive data collected or retained in the underlying logs.

prompt: A public information assistant sometimes presents generated claims without showing which approved source supports them. Which accountable process should the service team establish?
constraints: Users need to distinguish sourced facts from generated wording.
Unsupported claims can mislead the public.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Add a broad AI disclaimer and leave each public claim without a source or review owner.
Rely on the model provider’s general quality assurances instead of checking claims used by the service.
Measure average answer accuracy and let that metric replace review of disputed claims.
Assign a content owner to verify factual claims and escalate statements without evidence.

feedback.reason: A provenance check and accountable reviewer connect generated claims to evidence and provide a correction path. A generic launch approval or provider handoff does not resolve unsupported public statements.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Transparency makes the basis of an AI-generated result understandable, while accountability assigns people to review and correct unsupported claims.
details.scenarioApplication: A content owner should check claim provenance, make supporting sources visible where appropriate, and escalate unsupported or disputed statements for correction.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because a general disclaimer does not show whether a particular factual claim is supported.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Not every generated sentence needs a separate citation if it is clearly creative or non-factual; factual public claims require an evidence path.
details.transfer: When AI-generated content may be relied on as factual, make evidence review and correction ownership part of the publishing workflow.

messages.text: A general disclaimer does not show whether a particular factual claim is supported.
General provider assurances cannot establish the source for a specific statement shown to the public.
Aggregate accuracy does not reveal the evidence behind a specific unsupported statement.

prompt: A fraud-screening pilot produces a rise in false positives that delays legitimate customers. Which governance control should the operator put in place while the issue is investigated?
constraints: False-positive flags can delay legitimate transactions.
A human review team is available for disputed cases.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Assign a fraud owner to review flags, track false positives, and resolve disputes.
Keep automated holds in place until the next model update because the model team owns accuracy.
Transfer responsibility for customer disputes to the model provider that produced the score.
Wait for customers to contact support before reviewing the detected false-positive increase.

feedback.reason: The immediate risk is harm to legitimate customers, so an accountable owner and dispute path are needed alongside monitoring. Provider transfer or waiting for complaints leaves the impact unmanaged.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability connects observed harms to named people who can review cases, monitor the risk, and change the operating decision.
details.scenarioApplication: A fraud operations owner should review affected cases, monitor the false-positive signal, and define how disputes are escalated while the cause is investigated.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because model development ownership does not replace operational accountability for customers affected today.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A temporary review path can be limited to affected cases while evidence is gathered; it need not suspend every fraud control.
details.transfer: When an AI flag can burden a person, define who reviews disputes and how a rising harm signal changes reliance on the flag.

messages.text: Model development ownership does not replace operational accountability for customers affected today.
The provider may investigate the model, but the operator controls the hold and customer resolution.
The observed rise is already a reason to act; complaint-only review delays help for affected customers.

prompt: A translation assistant adds a language variety that was absent from the original evaluation. Early reviewer reports show more errors on eligibility notices in that variety. Which lifecycle action is most appropriate?
constraints: The new language variety was not represented in the earlier evaluation.
Errors affect notices used in eligibility decisions.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Rely on the original overall evaluation because it met the launch target before the language was added.
Name a language-risk owner to monitor eligibility errors and escalate unsafe new-cohort use.
Assume the model provider’s language coverage statement replaces local review of eligibility translations.
Wait until the language reaches the same traffic as larger cohorts before examining reported errors.

feedback.reason: A newly served language group and observed errors are concrete changes to the deployment context. Repeating the old overall score or vaguely revisiting the decision would not assign an actionable owner or signal.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Responsible lifecycle management reassesses risks when the intended use or affected population changes and assigns owners to monitor outcomes.
details.scenarioApplication: The language-service owner should add the new cohort to monitoring, review consequential translation errors, and escalate if the supported-use decision needs to change.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because the old evaluation did not represent this language variety and cannot answer how it performs now.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A small early sample supports focused review and evidence gathering, not a broad claim that the language is unusable.
details.transfer: When a new population or language enters use, name the owner who will review its outcomes and the signal that triggers escalation.

messages.text: The old evaluation did not represent this language variety and cannot answer how it performs now.
Coverage information does not establish error rates or accountability for this specific consequential use.
Early focused review can identify consequential problems without waiting for high traffic volume.

prompt: A content-moderation assistant removes some posts that reviewers later find compliant. Which operational accountability control should protect users while the removal pattern is investigated?
constraints: Removed posts can affect users’ ability to participate.
A human moderator can review appeals.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Use a monthly overall accuracy score and offer no case-level appeal unless the score falls.
Let the model provider decide appeals while the platform records only the original removal.
Assign a moderation owner to review appeals and escalate repeated overturned removals.
Keep removals final and ask users to submit general feedback about moderation quality.

feedback.reason: An appeal owner and an observable overturn signal address both individual impact and the recurring pattern. Waiting for unstructured complaints or deferring to the vendor leaves no reliable remedy.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Accountability provides a human review path for decisions with consequences and assigns an owner to monitor and respond to errors.
details.scenarioApplication: A moderation owner should make appeals reviewable, track overturned removals, and escalate a sustained error pattern for policy or system review.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because an aggregate score cannot resolve an individual wrongful removal or reveal whose posts are affected.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An appeal process can prioritize high-impact or time-sensitive cases while keeping ordinary moderation queues manageable.
details.transfer: For automated content restrictions, preserve a path to human reconsideration and assign someone to act on repeated reversals.

messages.text: An aggregate score cannot resolve an individual wrongful removal or reveal whose posts are affected.
The platform applies the restriction and must retain responsibility for reconsideration and user remedy.
General feedback does not provide a reviewable appeal or a reliable path to restore wrongly removed content.

prompt: A claims-processing pilot rejects model outputs that omit required fields. The rejection rate begins rising after a form change, delaying claim review. Which control should the operator define?
constraints: Schema rejection is measured before delivery to the claims system.
Rejected outputs delay downstream claim review.
Choose one answer.

options.text: Keep the validator and rely on the downstream system to absorb any increase in rejected claims.
Ask the form vendor to approve continued use without checking claim outcomes.
Wait for the quarterly model review before checking rejections caused by the recent form change.
Set a rejection-rate threshold; a named owner recovers cases, then escalates or rolls back if crossed.

feedback.reason: The rise is a concrete operational signal linked to a recent change. A named owner, affected-case review, and threshold make response auditable; schema validation alone only detects the failure.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Lifecycle accountability assigns owners to monitor operational risk, investigate changes, and define escalation or rollback when service outcomes degrade.
details.scenarioApplication: A claims operations owner should track the rejection rate after the form change, review affected claims, and trigger escalation or rollback at a defined threshold.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternative is incomplete because detection does not recover delayed cases or establish who responds to a rising failure rate.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The threshold should prompt investigation and possibly rollback; it should not silently discard claims or assume every rejection is a model defect.
details.transfer: When an integration change increases rejected decisions, connect the metric to a named owner, case recovery, and a reversible response.

messages.text: Detection does not recover delayed cases or establish who responds to a rising failure rate.
The vendor can explain the form change, but the claims operator remains accountable for downstream service.
A quarterly cadence is too slow to respond to an already rising operational failure signal.
